en:
Hello.
I'm Tomoharu Hosoda, Class 2-C.
Nice to meet you all.
I'll get right to the scary story, then... {a}{f:|}?
You go to the restroom, don't you?
Restrooms are scary, aren't they?
Even among scary stories about schools, the ones about restrooms are the most common.
I mean, in the restroom, the girls all use stalls, right?
And even boys use a stall when it's number two.{p}

That cramped, suffocating little space.
It's seriously scary.
Especially a restroom in the evening, when no one's around.
It's lonely, and a draft or something comes creeping in, whoosh... whoosh..., and it just feels wrong.
The door creaks open, and someone comes in.
But you can't tell who it is.
And then only their footsteps echo, clack... clack..., coming closer to you.
What if it were a killer...?{p}

You'd want to scream before you knew it, right?
I think that kind of psychology is at work, and that's how so many scary stories naturally came about.
But you know, lots of scary things really do happen in restrooms.
So, I'm going to tell you a story about those restrooms.
And so, I want to test you now.
...No, it's nothing weird.
People often tell me I have a strong sixth sense.
I end up seeing a lot of strange things.
And, well, I sense something in you that's the same as in me.
How should I put it... an aura, I guess?
Call it a signal, or a wavelength, but anyway, you and I seem like the same kind of person to me.
So I think if I'm with you, the spiritual aura will get even stronger.
So, um, would you go out with me for a bit?
When I ask you to go out with me, I don't mean it like that.
I mean there's somewhere I want you to go with me.
What do you say?{p}Won't you go out with me for a bit?
Go out with him
Don't go out with him

Great.
That makes me happy.
I knew you'd say that.
Well then, let's go right away.
Of course, I'd like all of you to come along too.
Oh, it's nowhere special.
It's the restroom. The restroom.
I was thinking we'd go on a little rest-{g}room tour of the new school building.
You see, there's a rumor that something strange appears in the new building's restrooms.
I'd really like to check it out together with {a}{f:|}.
If {a}{f:|} senses a spiritual aura from a restroom, let's all go inside together.
Well then, everyone, shall we go?{p}

...{a}{f:|}, first up is the restroom on the north side of the new building's first floor.
Well?
Do you feel anything?{p}If you do, tell me honestly.
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...This is the restroom on the south side of the new building's first floor.
Well?{p}Do you feel it this time?
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...I see.
You don't feel anything here either?
Hmm... I've decided to trust your sixth sense.
Well then, let's try the second floor.{p}

Actually, you know, there's a strange rumor about that last restroom.
I don't really feel much from it myself, though.
Well, it's just a rumor. Just a rumor.
...Okay, here we are.{p}

This is the restroom on the south side of the new building's second floor.
...What do you think?
Give me your honest opinion.
Take a really good look.
Well?{p}Do you feel anything?
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...I see.
You don't feel anything.
Then let's go on to the next one.
It can't be helped, after all.{p}

...No, it's not like I'm disappointed or anything.
It's just that I get a strange sensation from that restroom, even if it's only the tiniest bit.
I thought maybe... that's all.
My sixth sense isn't all that reliable anyway.
I think the mysterious aura you give off is far greater than mine, you see.{p}

...Okay, here we are.
This is the restroom on the north side of the new building's second floor.
How about it?
Can you see anything?
Isn't there some murky air hanging around in there?{p}I'd like to hear your straight opinion.
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...I see.
Of course not.
So there really is nothing in this restroom.
That's good.
What a relief.{p}

Well then, let's go to the third floor.
The third floor, you see, is overflowing with spiritual aura for some reason.
See, you feel it too, right?
The closer we get to the roof, the stronger the aura gets, for some reason.
That kind of phenomenon is supposed to be pretty rare, though. I wonder why.
...Still, this school sure is big.
Even though I go here myself, I get thoroughly sick of it.
...Hup, there we go.
Okay, here we are.{p}

This is the restroom on the north side of the new building's third floor.
See?
You feel it too, don't you?
The aura, swirling all around.
What do you think?
You don't have to be scared.
As long as you and I are together, the spirits won't attack us.
Come on, tell me.
Tell me how you really feel.
Well?{p}You clearly feel something, don't you?
I feel something
I don't feel anything

.........I see.
You don't feel it.
...I see.
No, don't worry about it.
Maybe you're the one who's right.
Maybe I'm the only one who feels a strong aura here.{p}

Well then, shall we go?
There's only one restroom left in the new building.
If you don't feel anything in that one either, then... maybe it means there really is nothing there after all.
We're almost there.
To tell you the truth, I can feel a tremendous aura coming from that restroom.
For someone like you, there's no doubt about it.
You're absolutely sure to feel it.{p}

I feel like with you here, I might get to see whatever is lurking in this restroom.
Come on, how about it?
You feel it, right?{p}You can feel that something is definitely lurking in this restroom, can't you?
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...You don't feel it?
You really don't feel it?
You're kidding, right?
Tell me honestly.{p}You really do feel it, don't you?
I feel something
I don't feel anything

...I see.
Oh well.
Then let's head back.
It wouldn't be fair to drag our seniors around any more than this.
Let's go back to the newspaper club and continue the stories.
"Um, wait a moment, please.
...I suddenly really need to use the restroom."
"Oh, okay.
Then we'll head back to the newspaper club, so come join us later."{p}

With that, Hosoda and the others went back to the newspaper club.
Hosoda was still tilting his head, looking puzzled.
Was it really so strange that I hadn't felt anything?
...Whoops, no time to be thinking about that.
I dashed into the restroom.{p}

Inside, the stifling smell of ammonia stung my nose.
School restrooms stink.
Holding my breath, I decided to do my business quickly.
I went to the nearest urinal and unzipped.
...Ahh, that feels good.{p}

Huh?
I heard a sound behind me.
What was that?
I turned around.{p}

...But no one was there.
Maybe it was the wind.
Or just my imagination.
Thinking so, I went to wash my hands.{p}

There it was again.
That sound, again.
This was strange.
It wasn't my imagination.
I turned around once more.{p}
...And I waited for the sound to come.

I hadn't misheard it.
I could definitely hear a sound.{p}

It came from inside the second stall from the right.
People often knock on a stall door from outside to check whether someone's in there.{p}

But a sound coming from inside a stall...
What was it?
Why would a sound like that be coming from in there?
It definitely wasn't my imagination.
I could hear it for sure.{p}
As if lured by something, I stood in front of the door the sound was coming from.{p}

Was someone knocking on it as a prank?
I could clearly feel my whole body trembling.
My teeth were chattering so hard I could hear them myself.
Was someone in there?
Was this what it meant to sense a spiritual aura?
I slowly reached out for the knob.
What should I do?
Open it?{p}Or run away?
Open it
Don't open it, just wait and see what happens
Run away

Even the hand gripping the knob was shaking badly.
The trembling that seized my whole body showed no sign of stopping.
I made up my mind to open the door.
I slowly turned the knob.{p}

There was a click, and when I pulled the door toward me, it moved slowly.
It wasn't locked...{p}

After that, the door opened on its own without my putting any strength into it.
Slowly, ever so slowly, the door swung open, laying bare the inside of the stall.{p}

...Huh?
There's nobody in here?
Should I really be relieved?
If there's nobody in here, then who was knocking on the door just now?
What was that sound coming from the inside?
Who on earth was knocking?{p}

"Whoa!"
I jumped back without thinking.
What's going on?!
What is this sound?!{p}
The doors of all the other stalls began to rattle at once with a tremendous noise.
The doors were shaking so violently they seemed about to break at any moment.
It was the sound of someone trapped inside, kicking wildly at the door in sheer terror.{p}

The sound of someone slamming their body against the door, desperate to get out somehow, echoed all through the restroom.
"Stop it!"
I had screamed before I knew it.
How wonderful it would have been if that had made the noise stop.
As if defying me, the noise only seemed to grow even more violent.{p}

It felt as if every drop of moisture in my body was gushing out as sweat.
Had I ever tasted terror like this before?
An unseen terror.
The terror of not being able to imagine what would happen next.
There was definitely something in this restroom.
But I didn't know what that something was.
The indescribable dread of coming face to face with a completely unknown, unfathomable presence.{p}

I felt dizzy.
I felt sick.
It was as if the air had solidified; I couldn't breathe properly.
It felt like being forced to swallow a lump the size of a golf ball.
I never knew breathing could be this hard...
My heart pounded, and I couldn't pull my thoughts together about what to do.
What should I do?{p}What can I do?
Scream
Knock back on the door
Run away
I ran for the door.

I grabbed the knob roughly and twisted it, rattling it as if I meant to wrench it right off.
...It won't open!

The knob won't turn!{p}As if it had been locked from the outside, the door wouldn't budge, no matter whether I pushed or pulled.
I was trapped in the restroom.{p}

"Open up!"
I screamed at the top of my lungs and pounded on the door like a madman.{p}
As if joining in with my screams, the pounding from inside the stalls grew even more violent.{p}

"Waaaaaaaah!"
I screamed without even knowing why.{p}

...The sound had stopped.
As if all that noise had never happened, silence came flooding in.{p}

"Waaah!"
It happened without warning.
With a crash like a hammer slamming into a door, every door flew open at once.
I craned my neck and peeked inside, ever so carefully.{p}

...Nothing there.
Calm down.
Just calm down.
I told myself that again and again.
I had to calm down and think of a way to get out of here.
Calm down.{p}What should I do?
Wash my face at the sink
Take a deep breath
Try turning the doorknob again

That's it.
I'll wash my face.
I can't let myself get scared.
That's right.
There's nothing to be scared of.
I have to show I'm not rattled.
Okay, I'll wash my face.{p}

Trying to ignore everything else, I headed for the sink.
The face in the mirror was as white as paper.
Is this really my face?
...Calm down.
Just calm down.{p}

I turned the faucet.
The water came gushing out.
Cold.
The ice-cold water snapped my jittery nerves back into place.
I scooped up water in my palms and buried my face in it.
...That feels good.
Little by little, I was calming down.
That's the way.
Yes, this is fine.
I filled my palms again and splashed my face hard.
The chill steadied my nerves even more.
Being scared is the problem.
It's because I'm scared that I see weird things.{p}
...Phew, that's refreshing.{p}

I raised my head and looked in the mirror.
Yeah, I've got more color than before.
I was gradually calming down.
...Huh?
What's that black shadow behind me in the mirror?
Some kind of hazy black shadow.
What is that?
Is something behind me?
...My legs started shaking again.
The shaking had finally stopped, and now my teeth began chattering again.
What is this presence?
A sickening feeling, like someone stroking my hair up from the roots.
A creeping revulsion, like someone stroking the nape of my neck.{p}

...I-I'll wash my face again.
I must have seen wrong.{p}

I only see weird things because I keep thinking how scared I am.
I thrust my hands into the water gushing from the faucet.
The splashing drops soaked my shirt.
I buried my face in the water once more.{p}
And now, to look in the mirror again.{p}

Nothing's there.
...Nothing's in the mirror.
Telling myself that, I raised my head and slowly opened my eyes.
Slowly, slowly, the mirror came into view.{p}

...Nothing's there.
I can't see anything.
...Only my own face is in the mirror.
See, I really did see wrong.
If I calm down and take a good look, there's nothing weird to see.
Thank goodness.
I'll wash my face once more.
Just to clear my head.{p}

............!
It happened the instant I looked down.
That was when I saw something strange in the sink.
Before I knew it, the sink had filled to the brim with water, and there was a human face in it.
With only the face poking out above the surface, a half-rotten face was staring right at me.
Its hair drifted and swayed.
Two eyeballs, ready to spill out at any moment, quivered as if about to be squeezed out of rims of rotten, mushy, melting flesh.
And then the face grinned.{p}
"Waaaaaaaaaah!"{p}

...I lost consciousness.
...How much time had passed?
"{a}! ...{a}!"
Someone was calling me.{p}

When I opened my eyes, that face was... no, it was Hosoda's face.
"Are you all right?
You never came back, so I got worried and came to check on you.
Did something happen?"
Something?
It was a lot more than something.
I didn't know how to answer him.{p}Hosoda was looking at me as if he were hoping for that something.
Say nothing happened
Tell him what just happened

"No, nothing really happened.
I just got a little dizzy and fell over.
Maybe all these scary stories had me so tense that I wore myself out..."
"...I see.
Well, as long as you're okay."
Hosoda looked disappointed.{p}

The restroom door was open.
The door that had been shut so tight now stood open, just like that.
If I was going to escape, it had to be now.
With Hosoda holding me up by the shoulder, I staggered out on unsteady legs and finally made it out of the restroom.
Hosoda murmured under his breath.{p}

"...Hey.
I still feel like there's something in this restroom, though..."
"No. There's nothing in there.
It's just your imagination."
I flatly brushed off what Hosoda said.{p}

"...Did you hear that just now?
That wasn't the wind, was it?"
"It was the wind.
Come on, let's hurry back.
There's no way ghosts exist."
I denied it stubbornly.
And I knew perfectly well it wasn't because I didn't believe, but because I didn't want to admit it.
Hosoda nodded as if he understood exactly how I felt.
"...I see.
No, you're right.
Actually, you know, I got locked in that restroom once myself.
That time, the doors kept banging back and forth, and I could hear these weird sounds..."
"Stop it!"
I didn't want to hear any more of Hosoda's story.
Maybe because I'd shouted without meaning to, Hosoda looked at me blankly.
But he soon smiled.
A knowing smile, as if he knew everything.
"...Oh, right.
It's just my imagination, isn't it?
...I think you and I are alike.
Very much alike, I think.
...Come on, let's hurry back to the newspaper club.
Everyone's waiting for us."{p}

That's right.
My job wasn't finished yet.
I trudged back to the newspaper club with heavy steps.
To hear the next scary story.{p}

Don't say that.
Then my story ends right here.
Please, I guarantee it'll make a really interesting article.
If I just tell it here, it'll only be half as scary, right?
Show a little curiosity, like a real newspaper club member.{p}
So, what do you say?

"Really★
So you do have a sixth sense!
Just as I thought.
Well then, shall we go right in?{p}

I'm sorry to ask, but would you upperclassmen mind waiting out in the hallway?"
Everyone murmured a little.
Hosoda went on.
"I really think it'll be easier for us both to sense something if it's just the two of us."
Then someone spoke up.
"Then there was no point in us coming along at all."
"No, I wanted you here so you could help us if anything happened.
Everyone!
Please, I'm asking for your cooperation."
Hosoda bowed his head to everyone.
Reluctantly, everyone stepped out into the hallway.{p}

"Now, {a}{f:|}, which stall do you sense the aura coming from?"
I should never, ever have said I sensed an aura.
I only said it because I had a vague feeling, that's all...
Right now, {f:I|I} really regret it...
{f:Hosoda|Interview or not}, {f:to put it bluntly, is fat|I can't believe I'm going into the boys' restroom}.
{f:If I get shut in a tiny closed space like this with him|If anyone finds out}, what {f:am I|am I} supposed to {f:do|do}?
Besides, {f:Hosoda has kind of a girly side to him|I have no idea what kind of person Hosoda is}.
What if he grabs my hand or something...
{f:Well|Nah}, I'm overthinking it{f:, right|, aren't I}? {f:Ha ha ha|Ahaha}.
"What are you laughing at?
Come on, let's go in."{p}

The boys' restroom on the north side of the new building's first floor has only two stalls.
At a glance there seem to be three{f:, but|, but} the one on the far right is a cleaning closet.
For now, {f:we decided|it was settled} that we'd go into the middle one.
First, Hosoda opened the door.{p}

A stifling reek of ammonia hung in the air.
"Go ahead, you first..."
At his urging, {f:I|I} went inside.
Then he came in after me, practically shoving {f:me|me} in.{p}

Shoving Hosoda out, I tumbled into the hallway.
Someone was looking at {f:me|me} with concern.
"{a}{f:|}, what's wrong★
Did something happen★
You're drenched in sweat.
And you look pale..."
{f:If I had to squeeze into a stall with someone,|......} {f:I wish it had been a girl...|I can't even muster the strength to answer.}{p}

"{a}{f:|} sensed a spirit in there just now and started feeling sick."
Hosoda told them.
The truth is, {f:it was all Hosoda's fault|that's not what happened at all}...
This time, {f:I|I}'ll just have to {f:grin and bear it|put up with it}.
"{f:I|I}'m fine, really... come on, let's hurry on to the next one."
I have to pull myself together and think of this as training to become a good newspaper club member...
Hosoda seemed {f:all fired up|really pumped}.{p}

...I see.
So you don't feel anything here.
Hmm... I've decided to trust your sixth sense.
Well then, let's try the second floor.{p}

This is the restroom on the south side of the new building's second floor.
...What do you think?
Give me your honest opinion.
Take a really good look.
Well?
Do you feel anything?{p}

"Whoa★
You sense something?
Great, I'm glad.
So, which stall is it coming from?"
Hosoda asked {f:me|me}, looking pleased with himself.{p}

"From that toilet over there..."
{f:I|I} pointed.
"Really? Then let's go in together."
Hosoda {f:looked|seemed} {f:delighted|so happy}.
Just then,{p}

"Sorry, but would you go in with me instead?"
Fukuzawa cut in from the side.
{f:Score|Yay}! I don't have to go in with Hosoda.
"But... well, all right."
Hosoda {f:seemed|seemed} to give in to Fukuzawa's pushiness.
"Come on, {c}{f:|}, let's go in together."
At Fukuzawa's urging, {f:I|I} went into the stall.{p}

With a click, she locked the stall.
"Do you sense something too, Fukuzawa?"
{f:I|I} asked.
Since Fukuzawa's in the same year as me, I {f:feel|feel} more at ease with her.
"I sense it...
I sense a powerful spirit here."
Fukuzawa was trembling as she said it.{p}

"Urgh☆"
Suddenly she spewed a huge load of vomit from her mouth into the toilet.
Then, slowly, she raised her face...
Her eyes had rolled back to the whites.{p}

Then her whole body began to shudder.
Little by little her trembling grew worse.
"Uuugh, uuuugh, uuuuuuuuugh!"
She {f:seemed|seemed} to have fallen into a trance.
With her blocking the way out, {f:I|I} {f:could only|had no choice but to} watch her bizarre behavior from the corner of the stall.
"Scritch, scritch, scritch..."
Then I noticed another sound mixed in with her strange cries.
"Ugh!"
When {f:I|I} looked down, I nearly fainted.{p}

"Uuugh, uuuugh, uuuuuuuuugh!"
She was {f:still|still} stuck in that same state.{p}

{f:I|I} squeezed my eyes shut.
I'm going to lose my mind☆
The instant I thought that...
She grabbed {f:me|me} by the shoulder.{p}

When I slowly looked up, there was her face, smiling sweetly.
"So, how was it?
That was fun, wasn't it?"
She smiled as she said it.
She was completely back to normal.
"What on earth is going on...?"
{f:I|I} asked her.
"I just asked the spirit here to show you a fun little dream, {c}{f:|}."
"★"
She went on.
"Sometimes when I concentrate, I can make contact with spirits.
You went and said you sensed a spirit, {c}{f:|}, when you didn't believe it at all...
So I thought I'd play a little prank on you!
Hee hee hee!"
That's {f:insane, there's no way that really happened|ridiculous......}☆
She pointed at her wristwatch and said,
"It may have felt long, but it's only been fifteen seconds since then."
{f:I|I} went limp.
Whether what she said was a lie or the truth, it didn't matter anymore.
I just wanted to get out of here, fast.
I feel {f:sick|so sick}.{p}

"Oh, are you okay?"
She rubbed {f:my|my} back.
Ah!
Don't rub it...
If you rub it, it'll only...
"{f:Bleeeeeegh|Mm... urk}"
{f:Too late...|I'm about to throw up...}{p}

"Oh dear, you're hopeless.
{f:Throwing up this much|Making a face like that over something this small}.
{f:Don't tell me|Oh, what am I going to do with you}, {f:is this one of those sympathy pukes|shall we head back to the club room already}?
{f:Ahahahaha|Kyahahaha}"
She {f:laughed in my face as she said it|seemed to be having a great time}.{p}

When she unlocked the stall, she told everyone,
"{a}{f:|} sensed way too many spirits and {f:threw up|started feeling sick}.
Come on, we'd better not stay here.
Let's hurry back to the club room!"
{f:I|I}-{f:I'm|I'm}... never trusting her again, ever☆{p}

"A spirit... you sense a spirit?
I see, so which stall is it coming from?"
Hosoda asked {f:me|me}, looking pleased with himself.
"From that toilet over there..."
{f:I|I} pointed.
"Really? Then let's go in together."
Hosoda {f:looked|seemed} {f:delighted|so happy}.
Just then, Shindo cut in from the side.{p}

"Sorry, but let me go in instead.
I'm the upperclassman here, so you'll step aside, right?"
{f:Score|Yay}! I don't have to go in with Hosoda.
"But... well, all right."
Hosoda {f:seemed|seemed} to give in to Shindo's pushiness.
"{a}, let's go in."
At Shindo's urging, {f:I|I} went into the stall.{p}

With a click, he locked the stall.
Shindo looked all around the inside of the stall, then suddenly stopped moving.
And then he didn't move at all.
"...What's wrong?"
{f:I|I} asked him.
He didn't answer {f:my|my} question; he just stood there, stock-still.{p}

Silence went on...
Even so, he {f:must have had|surely had} something on his mind.
{f:I|I} decided to keep him company for a while.
Little by little, I could feel saliva pooling in {f:my|my} mouth.
{f:I|I} swallowed without meaning to.
"Gulp."
Oh, no!
I never thought it would be that loud...{p}

{f:I|I} glanced at Shindo.
He slowly turned to look at {f:me|me} as well.
Shindo smiled and said,
"Hey, take a look down there."
{f:I|I} looked down as he told me to.{p}

"Truth is, I've taken a liking to you.
Figured I'd take you along with me."
Shindo had lost his mind!
"{f:Somebody help me|Help}!"
{f:I|I} screamed on reflex.
"Hahaha, screaming won't do you any good.
Everyone's asleep right out there."
That's what he said.
The next moment, {f:I|I} gasped.{p}

What stood in front of {f:me|me} wasn't Shindo, but a cockroach in human form.
The cockroach was twirling its antennae round and round.
Its glistening black skin and the jagged spikes on its arms were sickeningly vivid.
"I've taken control of this guy's body.
Most of the time I still keep a human form.
But once I've fully merged with him, I'll never go back to human form again.
Fwahahaha!"
That's what {f:the thing|the cockroach} said.
Then... would Shindo's body someday stay like this and never return to normal{f:?|?}
I couldn't just leave Shindo like this{f:.|.}
{f:I've got to be brave!|I have to be brave!}☆{p}

{f:I|I} steeled myself and tackled him hard.
"Gwagh!"
As he staggered, something hazy burst out of his mouth and nose.
The hazy thing floated in the air for a while, then quickly vanished down the hole in the toilet.{p}

"Uh... uhhh..."
Now that the strange thing had left him, Shindo seemed to be back to his original form.
"Shindo, pull yourself together!☆"
"Why am I lying here?"
Shindo said.
Apparently he had no memory of the time he'd taken on {f:that thing's|that} form.
{f:I|I} unlocked the stall and hurried to drag Shindo out.{p}

Then I woke up everyone who was lying there.
"Let's get out of here, quick!"
{f:I|I} hurried everyone along.
With a bad feeling, {f:I|I} looked back...
And there...{p}
"{f:Aaaaaaaaagh|Eeeeeeeeek}!"{p}

We all rushed out into the hallway and slammed the restroom door shut as hard as we could.
Having lost their target, the cockroaches rustled and scrabbled on the other side of the door.
"Let's hurry back to the club room!☆"
{f:We|We} ran off in a blind frenzy.
At that moment, {f:I|I} felt a sense of mission as a member of the newspaper club.
